text:
maria: quick note — ran a small e2e where we split tenant namespaces across 'hosted-gpu' and 'dedicated-gpu' node pools in staging to validate eviction isolation. saw weird autoscaler churn when dedicated pool hit capacity :thinking:

alex: what kind of churn? did pods go PENDING or were nodes flapping?

maria: mostly PENDING plus a few pod restarts. cluster-autoscaler spawned nodes but then scale-down probed and autoscaler thought nodes were empty and drained them quickly, which kicked workloads back to PENDING. cost + instability spike.

tim: that sounds like scaleDownDelay/UnneededTime being too aggressive for our GPU workloads. GPUs get claimed slowly due to binpacking. what are the autoscaler flags in staging?

maria: using CA flags: --scale-down-unneeded-time=1m, --scale-down-unready-time=2m for the experiment. also using the random expander (we patched it to prefer cheapest first).

jun: random expander + short unneeded time = trouble. GPUs are expensive to launch; if CA decides a recently-created node is "empty" because pods are pending or waiting for PVs, it might try to remove it. We should set --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m and --balance-similar-node-groups to true for dedicated pools.

sylvia: also check taints/tolerations. Are tenant pods tolerating both hosted and dedicated taints? If we intended strict isolation, misconfigured tolerations could make CA move things around.

maria: good call. this is the pod spec we used for the dedicated namespace (trimmed):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-test
  namespace: tenant-dedicated
spec:
  containers:
  - name: worker
    image: our-inference:staging
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu.dedicated"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeSelector:
    pool: "dedicated-gpu"
```

alex: looks fine. what about node taints?

maria: nodes in dedicated pool have taint: gpu.dedicated=true:NoSchedule. hosted pool has no taint.

tim: two follow-ups: 1) bump CA scale-down thresholds and set max-node-provision-time to something higher for GPU groups, 2) ensure CA has stable scale-up timers (avoid preemptible/spot mix for dedicated).

jun: +1. also consider using a custom node-group auto-scaler profile per nodepool (we can run a second CA instance targeting labels like cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=dedicated-gpu) so CA decisions are pool-scoped. that prevents cross-pool churn.

sylvia: can we also tag these nodes in billing so we can correlate cost vs churn? want to see if the cost of longer warm-up > savings from aggressive scale-down.

maria: already added an internal dashboard entry: https://go/redwood/infra-dashboard/gpu-siloing (staging) — shows per-pool launch times and pod P90 queue times.

infra-bot: deployment triggered: updated CA flags in staging -> --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, --max-node-provision-time=15m. Rollout id: deploy-2026-03-10-187.

alex: nice. can you also add a prewarm policy for tenant-dedicated so we always keep 1 spare node for that pool? it avoids cold-start spikes.

maria: will do. thinking: keep 1 warm node for each dedicated tenant pool, and a burst pool for single-pod spikes. we should test with loadgen.

tim: when you test, include network attach times — we've seen slow CNI plugin + PV attach combine to keep pods in Pending long after node exists. that confuses CA heuristics.

maria: good point. will include CNI/PV in the replay. also will run a variant where dedicated pools run with "DoNotEvict" annotation for critical workloads so kubelet won't kubelet-evict them during scale-down decisions.

jun: we should document this as a recommended pattern: (1) pool-scoped autoscaler or dedicated CA, (2) conservative scale-down timing for GPU pools, (3) explicit taints/tolerations and node selectors for isolation, (4) small prewarm reserve, (5) per-pool billing tags + observability.

sylvia: can you put a short RFC in /docs or a PR in infra playbooks? i'll help with cost calc.

maria: filing RFC now: https://go/redwood/rfcs/tenant-gpu-siloing-experiment. will paste test results in this thread when done. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — this should help reduce noisy evictions and make dedicated pools truly predictable. :eyes:
